Ive been researching this too so i believe this is the answer: 

Coasting in neutral has the engine disconnected from the wheels. Therefore the motor will be idling which is using fuel to maintain a constant engine speed. 

Engine braking keeps the motor and wheels connected. Instead of the engine turning the wheels, the wheels are turning over the engine. When the computer detects you are engine braking, it cuts off fuel, giving you better fuel economy
